text:
anya: heads-up: onboarding failures with proxyless tenants when controlplane briefly partitions. agents keep using cached certs and some endpoints accept them for several minutes. need a defendable design to minimize blast while keeping availability.

carlos: quick idea: lease tokens issued with short TTL that must be renewed by agent. if CP unreachable, agent can keep working until lease expiry. revoked leases get tombstoned on manifest so agents refuse immediately.

emily: love lease idea. how do we propagate revokes quickly to NATed agents? polling every 30s at 10k tenants is noisy. we could use long-poll with server-sent events over the existing mux where possible, falling back to short-poll.

raj: long-poll + delta log looks pragmatic. manifest contains watermark/version + small list of ops: {revoke: leafID, rotate: newKeyID}. agent applies ops idempotently. ensure each op signed with CP key id + timestamp.

anya: also think about the offline window: if we make leaf TTL 3m and lease TTL 1m, an agent that misses CP for 4m will drop traffic; acceptable for most customers but risky for edge cases. we should document SLA impact.

carlos: for Dedicated deployments we should allow customer-local signers to issue lease tokens. include signer metadata in manifest and validate against allowed key list provisioned at onboarding.

emily: security: add monotonic sequence number per tenant so replayed manifests are rejected. include a nonce for initial bootstrap to avoid TOFU replay.

raj: performance thought: for 10k agents, 30s poll = ~1k req/s. with long-poll and a 5m heartbeats we get ~34 req/s avg. delta approach reduces bundle sizes. estimate: manifest ~1KB, delta ~200B.

ops-bot: alert: several tenants saw failed refresh counts spike to 0.8% during last CP deploy window.

anya: good to know. operationally we need these metrics: refresh-latency, last-known-version-per-tenant, stale-accepts, emergency-revoke-count. Also an incident runbook that explains how to set the tenant to "quarantine" forcing immediate disconnects.

carlos: API sketch:
```
GET /v1/tenants/:tid/manifest -> {version: 123, seq: 456, leases: [{id, ttl}], ops: [], signer: {key_id}}
GET /v1/tenants/:tid/delta?from_seq=456 -> [op1, op2]
POST /v1/tenants/:tid/ack -> {seq: 789}
```

emily: agents should ACK seq on apply. CP keeps a small ack window to allow replay safety. if agent reuses old ack, CP returns mismatch.

raj: a nuance: what if CP has multiple replicas? require centralized signing authority (KMS) and only accept manifests signed by keys in the trusted keyset. replicas can't issue without KMS RPC. reduces risk of inconsistent views.

anya: for emergency revokes we add a fast-path header check on connection establishment: agent sends last_seq; server replies with {blocked: true, seq: N} if tenant is globally quarantined. that avoids waiting for TTL.

ops-bot: note: add test for simulated network partitions to canary suite.

carlos: one more UX: expose a tenant-level "force-rotate" that stamps a new seq and returns a single small op so agents pick it up quickly. useful for suspected key compromise.

emily: we'll need to measure read QPS and signing latency for the KMS path. also consider batch-signing manifests when doing mass rotates.

anya: ok action items: carlos -> draft manifest + lease schema; emily -> long-poll client pattern + metrics; raj -> security/KMS doc; i'll tie into runaway SLOs and ops playbook. follow-up 30m next Tue. :eyes:
